title: The Spend-By Date
note: МАКЕТ. Сценарий, тексты и веса — наши. Ни одного числа, имени и формулировки PrepMatter (Ф3). Развилки ветвят по РОДУ хода (Ф21). Связывающее ограничение — ДЕНЬГИ С ДАТОЙ: грант сгорает и возвращается, если построенное не работает десять лет.

intro.head: Welcome to the Sustainable Futures Lab
intro.body: You have joined a small team advising a social housing landlord. You will make thirteen decisions. There is one clock for all of them, and you cannot go back.

intro.head: Background
intro.body: The Ashgate estate is eleven blocks, four hundred and twenty flats, all heated electrically and all in fuel poverty statistics. Thirteen months ago the landlord won a decarbonisation grant of six million to put solar and battery storage on the roofs. Three conditions came with it: the money must be invoiced and the equipment installed within twenty-four months of award, eleven of which are left; the installation must deliver at least sixty per cent of its projected annual output for ten years, or the grant is repaid pro rata; and the savings must reach tenants, not the landlord. Nothing has been ordered. The previous project manager left in the spring.
intro.mission: Your mission: get equipment installed and running inside eleven months, on terms the estate can still meet in year nine.

priorities.label: Form a view on which package can actually be installed inside eleven months
Settle with the grant office what counts as installed and what triggers repayment
Take the tenants’ association through what a ten-year guarantee asks of them
Work through the block-by-block consumption data before sizing anything

steps.prompt: Put these four actions in the order you would take them, starting with the one you would do first.
steps.why:
Связывающее здесь — **деньги с датой**, и это новое ограничение для библиотеки. В «District Heat Handover» календарь был законный и внешний: восемь месяцев консультации нельзя сократить, но потерять нельзя ничего, кроме времени. Здесь просроченная дата **забирает шесть миллионов обратно**, а построенное не по правилам забирает их через девять лет.
Первой идёт грантовая контора, и вот почему. «Установлено» означает либо акт и счёт, либо подключение и выработку — разница между этими двумя прочтениями **три месяца программы из одиннадцати**. Пока прочтение не названо, слова «успеваем» не существует: одна и та же схема успевает по первому чтению и не успевает по второму. Письмо в контору стоит день, а меняет содержание следующего шага целиком: под первое прочтение проходит один набор пакетов, под второе — другой. Первым идёт не самое срочное, а то, без чего второе решается вслепую.
Возражение сильное и его надо назвать: **спрашивать в пустоте бессмысленно, у конторы нет мнения о пакете, которого нет**. Оно верно ровно наполовину. Вопрос «акт или подключение» родовой: он не про пакет, он про то, что контора считает выполнением, и ответ на него одинаков для всех трёх пакетов. Родовой вопрос задаётся первым, вопрос про конкретный пакет — потом.
Отсюда второй — техническая картина того, что физически монтируется за оставшиеся месяцы: она отсекает большую часть вариантов сама, но отсекает по-разному в зависимости от первого ответа.
Жильцы третьими не потому, что менее важны, а потому что их согласие ничего не переопределяет: оно идёт своим ходом и от него не меняется ни один из первых двух ответов. Данные последними: неверный размер стоит денег и исправляется, пропущенная дата не исправляется ничем.

feedback.top: Your order settles what “installed” means before deciding what is buildable, and the second question changes with the answer to the first. Everything else runs alongside.
feedback.mid: Defensible, and at least one of the two items that gate the order of equipment is near the front. The estate will get something installed.
feedback.low: Your order studies the estate before establishing what counts as done and what can be built. The data will be excellent and the money will be gone.

steps.prompt: The tenants’ association has been told about this project twice before, by two managers who both left. Their chair opens the first meeting by asking what is different this time.

options.text: You answer that nothing is different yet, give the date the money expires, and say what you will have decided by the next meeting.
options.fb: The only thing you have that your predecessors did not is a date, and you used it. A promise with a deadline attached is the one kind this room has not heard twice already.

options.text: You set out the full plan for the estate and the savings each block should expect.
options.fb: It is the third full plan this room has been shown. The two before it were also complete and also true on the day they were given.

options.text: You ask the chair what the last two managers promised, so that whatever you say tonight is at least not the third version of the same sentence.
options.fb: A good question, and it costs the first meeting: the room came to hear something and leaves having told you things. Ask it second, not first.

options.text: You apologise for the two false starts and commit to monthly written updates whatever happens.
options.fb: The apology is owed and the updates are cheap. Neither answers the question the chair actually asked, which was about this project, not about your manners.

steps.prompt: Three packages are on the table: roof solar alone, solar with a shared battery per block, and solar with a battery in each flat. Nobody has been on the roofs since the estate was surveyed eleven years ago, and the structural report will take five weeks.

options.text: You rule out the in-flat batteries now on install time alone, since four hundred and twenty separate fit-outs is not an eleven-month job, and carry the other two into the survey.
options.fb: That judgement needed no survey: the constraint you already had was enough to remove a third of the field. Narrowing early is what leaves time to choose properly between the two that are left.

options.text: You wait for the structural report before ruling anything in or out, since roof loading decides what can go up there.
options.fb: Roof loading decides between the two solar packages. It says nothing about the in-flat option, and five weeks of the eleven months go to a question that was already answerable.

options.text: You pick roof solar alone now, because it is the one package that certainly fits the time and the roofs will carry it whatever the survey says.
options.fb: Fast and safe, and it gives away the storage that turns midday generation into savings for flats that are empty at midday. Certainty about the date bought at the price of the tenants’ half of the grant.

steps.prompt: The grant agreement says the money must be “invoiced and installed” by the deadline. Your contractor reads that as equipment on site and invoiced. Your finance director reads it as commissioned and generating. The difference is about three months of programme.

options.text: You put both readings to the grant office in writing and ask which one they will audit against, since only their reading decides.
options.fb: A three-month difference is not a question to settle by reading. You asked the party whose reading counts, and before the order rather than after it.

options.text: You design to the stricter reading, so the programme is safe whichever way the office would have ruled.
options.fb: Safe, and it spends three of the eleven months buying certainty you might have been given for the price of a letter you never sent.

options.text: You adopt the contractor’s reading, since it is the ordinary meaning of the words and the one the industry uses, and record it in the design file with your reasons.
options.fb: The ordinary meaning of the words is not the test; the office’s meaning is. A reading kept in your own design file protects nobody who has to repay six million.

B1a.prompt: The office answers: installed means energised and metered, but a meter reading may be taken up to sixty days later. In the same week the estate’s consumption file arrives — eleven blocks of half-hourly data, two of them rebuilt last year and running at a quarter of the rest.

options.text: You size on the nine unchanged blocks and give the two rebuilt ones a figure of their own.
options.fb: Two blocks with new fabric are not the same estate as the other nine. Averaged in, they would have undersized nine roofs and oversized two.

options.text: You use the full estate average, since the grant was awarded to the estate as a whole and will be judged that way.
options.fb: The grant is for the estate; the panels go on individual roofs and generate against individual demand. An average that no block matches sizes nothing correctly.

options.text: You ask the supplier to re-issue the file with the rebuilt blocks flagged, and hold the sizing until it comes.
options.fb: The flag is already visible in the numbers, because you spotted it yourself. Waiting for someone to write down what you can see costs weeks you are counting.

B1b.prompt: Nobody has asked the grant office anything: the reading the programme is built on is your own. In the middle of the design the contractor’s roof survey lands, and it measures usable roof area on seven blocks as materially smaller than the asset register says — and the register is what the application was costed on.

options.text: You have three roofs re-measured by a third party, because one of the two numbers is wrong and neither side is neutral.
options.fb: The grant was costed on the older figure and the newer one comes from the party being paid by the area. Three roofs is enough to tell you which is right, and cheap next to redesigning on the wrong one.

options.text: You take the contractor’s survey as correct, since it is the recent measurement, it was made for this job, and the register has not been touched in eleven years.
options.fb: Recent and purpose-made is a good prior, and a contractor measuring the area he is paid to cover is not a neutral source. Prior is not proof.

options.text: You keep the asset register figure, because the grant application and its budget are built on it.
options.fb: The application does not put panels on roofs. If the register is wrong, the shortfall appears in year one of a ten-year output guarantee.

steps.prompt: The savings can be passed to tenants two ways. A flat monthly credit is simple and identical for everyone. A tariff that follows generation gives the biggest saving to whoever uses power in the middle of the day — which on this estate means the people at home all day, most of them retired or unwell.

options.text: You propose the generation-following tariff with a floor, and pay for the floor by capping the largest daytime shares.
options.fb: The pool is fixed, so the floor comes out of the top of it: the biggest daytime users gain less than the pure tariff would have given them. That is the trade, you made it deliberately, and you said out loud who pays.

options.text: You propose the flat credit, because an identical benefit is the one nobody in the association can argue against and the one the housing team can administer without a new system.
options.fb: It will pass the meeting, and it hands the same amount to a flat that is empty all day as to one that is not. Simplicity bought with a weaker match to the estate.

options.text: You propose the generation-following tariff and explain the logic at the association meeting.
options.fb: The logic is right and half the room hears that their neighbours will do better than them. Explained fairness is not the same as fairness that needs no explanation.

options.text: You let the association choose between the two, presenting both with numbers.
options.fb: You have given a mixed room a choice in which one group gains and another does not, and no proposal of your own. The meeting will settle it by who speaks loudest.

steps.prompt: Access scaffolding goes up on the first two blocks for the structural survey. Within a week the association reports that the survey crews have been leaving the stair doors propped open, and one has been smoking on a walkway. The survey is running three weeks ahead of programme.

options.text: You raise it with the contractor as a programme risk, not a courtesy issue, and agree a named site supervisor the association can call.
options.fb: Access to the roofs runs through people who live under them, and you will be back on this estate for months with far more equipment. Framing it as programme risk is what makes it move; a name to call is what stops the next complaint reaching you as a rumour.

options.text: You apologise to the association and ask the contractor to remind the crews.
options.fb: A reminder against a crew that is three weeks ahead of programme has a short life, and this crew leaves before the installers arrive. You spent the complaint without buying anything with it.

options.text: You point out that the survey crews are three weeks ahead of schedule and ask the association for patience for the few weeks they are on the block.
options.fb: You have told people whose doors are being propped open that the schedule matters more than their front door. The next access request goes to a meeting instead of a phone call.

options.text: You put a site supervisor of your own on the estate for the duration of the works.
options.fb: It solves the problem and it puts your own cost against a contractor obligation. Right instinct, wrong pocket, and it will be there for eleven months.

steps.prompt: Panel prices have moved. Your supplier will hold the current price for ten days against a firm order for the whole estate; after that the quote is re-issued monthly. The structural report is in for eight blocks and outstanding for three.

options.text: You order for the eight surveyed blocks now and leave the other three to a second order at whatever price comes.
options.fb: Eight blocks of certainty at a held price and three of exposure is the split the information actually supports. You bought what you knew and left open what you did not.

options.text: You let the ten days pass and order once all eleven structural reports are in, at whatever the quote says by then.
options.fb: Complete information, paid for at next month’s price on eleven blocks instead of three. Defensible, and the more expensive way to be right.

options.text: You ask the supplier to extend the hold, and build the programme on the extension being granted.
options.fb: The supplier has no reason to hold a price for a customer whose deadline is public in the grant register. Planning on a favour is not a plan.

B2a.prompt: The eight blocks are on order. The projection in the grant application is stated as annual output per kilowatt installed, and the total in it was that figure multiplied by the array the application assumed — larger than the eight now ordered plus the three still to come.

options.text: You restate the total against the array actually ordered and take the new number to the grant office yourself.
options.fb: The per-kilowatt figure never changed and the thing it was multiplied by did. The sixty per cent is measured against the total in the file, so the total in the file has to be the one you are building.

options.text: You keep the application total, since the per-kilowatt figure it was built on is still correct, still current, and still the manufacturer’s own.
options.fb: A correct rate against the wrong quantity is a wrong answer. In year two somebody divides real output by that total and the ratio is not sixty per cent.

options.text: You keep the application total and plan to make the difference up on the three blocks still to be ordered.
options.fb: You have decided to say nothing and to fix it with roofs whose reports are not in, at a price nobody has quoted. Of the ways to keep a wrong number in a grant file, this is the one that never gets corrected.

options.text: You raise it with the grant office only if the final three blocks do not close the gap.
options.fb: At least the disclosure exists, with a condition in front of it. The gap is arithmetic you can do today, and waiting turns a correction into a confession the office dates from when you first knew.

B2b.prompt: The hold expires with nothing ordered, and the new quote comes back with a different panel model — the first is out of stock at this volume. Its output is stated under a different test standard than the model everything was compared against, and on paper it looks four per cent better.

options.text: You have both models restated under one standard before anything is signed.
options.fb: Four per cent between two standards is not four per cent between two panels. One number restated is a morning’s work; the wrong panel is on the roofs for a decade.

options.text: You accept the four per cent, since the newer standard is the stricter of the two and the figure is therefore conservative.
options.fb: Stricter in general is not stricter for this shape of roof and this latitude. A direction of travel is not a conversion.

options.text: You keep the original model and wait for stock, holding the programme.
options.fb: Waiting for stock is waiting on a warehouse you do not control, in the months you have left. The panel was never the scarce thing here.

options.text: You ask the installer which of the two he would put on his own roof, and take that.
options.fb: He will name the one he can get, fit fastest and service most cheaply. All three are reasonable to him and none of them is the ten-year output guarantee you signed.

steps.prompt: The grant office offers a variation: an extra four months on the deadline, in exchange for the ten-year output condition becoming twelve years. It wants an answer this week.

options.text: You ask for a shorter extension at the ten-year condition, and say you will take the four months if that is the only shape on offer.
options.fb: Time is the thing this programme is short of, so the extension is worth having. Asking for the version without the tail, while making clear you are not refusing it, is how you find out whether the tail was ever the point.

options.text: You take the four months as offered and tell the board the condition now runs two years longer.
options.fb: Real float bought at a real price, and the price falls on a landlord two post-holders from now. Defensible; you paid the asking price without testing it.

options.text: You decline the extension and say the programme does not need it.
options.fb: Declining reads as confidence and leaves you with whatever room you already had, which on a programme of this length is not much. Confidence is not a schedule.

options.text: You take the extension and use the time to widen the scheme to the roofs left out of it.
options.fb: Two more years of liability spent on scope rather than on safety. The extension has become a reason to grow the job rather than a reason to finish it.

steps.prompt: In the last months the orders come in above the figure the application was costed on. The gap is roughly the price of everything that goes indoors — storage where the scheme kept it, switchgear and inverters where it did not. Nothing can be added to the grant, and nothing bought after the deadline is paid for by it.

options.text: You put everything that needs scaffolding and a roof into the works now, and defer whatever can be carried into a plant room later.
options.fb: Access is what the programme is buying: scaffolding, roofs and an electrician on them. What fits through a door can be bought later out of the operating share — not out of the grant, and that is the trade you are making with your eyes open.

options.text: You cut the indoor scope back to the bare minimum the installation needs to run, and put everything the cut releases into panels on the roofs.
options.fb: Output is protected and everything the indoor equipment was there to add — storage where the scheme has it, headroom everywhere else — goes. One condition defended, the tenants’ half quietly traded for it.

options.text: You ask the landlord’s board to fund the gap from reserves and keep the scheme whole.
options.fb: Legitimate, and a board runs on its own calendar while the deadline runs on the grant’s. Ask — but not as the only plan you have.

options.text: You reduce the number of panels per roof so the indoor scope survives at full size.
options.fb: Panels are the output the sixty per cent is measured on. You protected the part that is not in the grant condition by cutting the part that is.

steps.prompt: The output condition — ten years, or twelve if you took the variation — needs an owner. If output falls below sixty per cent in any year, the grant is repaid pro rata. Maintenance, inverter replacement and roof access for all of it sit behind that number.

options.text: The landlord carries it, funded by a ring-fenced share of the generation before any credit is paid out.
options.fb: The party that signed the grant carries the condition, and the money for it comes off the top rather than from a line that will be argued about four years in.

options.text: The installer carries it under a performance contract for the full length of the condition, priced into the works.
options.fb: The cleanest allocation on paper, and it rests on one contractor still trading near the end of it. If they are not, the condition comes back with the maintenance history in somebody else’s filing system.

options.text: The tenants’ association carries it through a service charge, since the savings go to tenants.
options.fb: You have moved the whole liability from a landlord with reserves onto households in fuel poverty. The saving was the point of the grant; the liability was never theirs.

B3a.prompt: Eleven days before the deadline you are working to, the works are done. Then the network operator confirms that two of the roofs cannot be switched on for another three weeks: their meter exchanges fall outside the window it can offer.

options.text: You notify the grant office before the date, give the energisation dates and ask them to treat the meter reading as completion for those two blocks.
options.fb: Asked before the date this is a variation; the same words after it are an explanation of a breach. Anyone who settled the meaning of “installed” back in month one already knows the answer they will get.

options.text: You wait until the two blocks are energised and report the completed scheme in one submission.
options.fb: A complete submission arriving after the date reads as a scheme that missed it. Whatever allowance existed was worth something only while there was still a date to be early for.

options.text: You ask the metering contractor to certify the two blocks as energised on the deadline date and correct it later.
options.fb: That is a false certificate on a grant file, and it converts a three-week programme issue into a fraud question about six million.

options.text: You de-scope the two blocks to protect the submission and add them later at the landlord’s cost.
options.fb: It protects the date and costs two blocks their place in the scheme plus the landlord the money the grant was meant to spend. A safe answer that pays twice.

B3b.prompt: Installation finishes eleven days before the deadline you are working to, and the party that agreed to carry the output condition has not signed yet. It asks to see the maintenance regime it is guaranteeing, and no regime has been written. Two blocks will also not be energised until three weeks after the deadline.

options.text: You write the regime this week from the design, and notify the grant office of the energisation dates before the deadline rather than after.
options.fb: Both are cheap this week and expensive in a fortnight. A condition nobody has written down is a condition nobody owns, and a late notification is the same fact read as a breach.

options.text: You notify the office about the two blocks and leave the regime to the first year of operation.
options.fb: The urgent half is done. The half you left is what the carrying party is signing against, and it will be reopened by whoever is in post when the first inverter fails.

options.text: You write the regime carefully over the next month and report the completed scheme to the office once both blocks are energised.
options.fb: Good work on the part with years to run and none on the part with eleven days. Order matters more here than either piece.

options.text: You ask them to sign now and settle the regime afterwards, since the deadline is the pressing thing.
options.fb: They are being asked to guarantee an obligation whose content is blank. A signature on that is worth what the blank is worth.

intro.head: Welcome to the Sustainable Futures Lab
intro.body: You have joined a small team advising a farmer-owned creamery. You will make thirteen decisions. There is one clock for all of them, and you cannot go back.

intro.head: Background
intro.body: Larnwick Creamery is owned by three hundred and twelve dairy farms and turns their milk into cheese in a valley served by a single gas main. The gas network in the valley has been approved for closure in twenty months, four of which have already gone; after that there is no gas at any price. Electric boilers would need about two and a half times the site's present connection of 750 kilovolt-amperes, and the network operator's published queue gives the creamery a date four years out. Queue places cannot be bought. They move when an applicant ahead withdraws, or when the capacity asked for falls under the threshold that lets a job be treated as small works and leave the queue altogether. Two of the applicants ahead are neighbours the farms will still be living beside in ten years.
intro.mission: Your mission: have the creamery making cheese on the day the gas goes off, without a place in the queue you cannot honestly hold.

priorities.label: Work out which parts of the plant can live under a smaller connection than the one you asked for
Get the network operator to say in writing what a reduced ask does to your place in the queue
Put the position to the farmer members before anything is given up on their behalf
Go through the half-hourly records to see what the site actually draws

steps.prompt: Put these four actions in the order you would take them, starting with the one you would do first.
steps.why:
Связывающее здесь — **место в чужой очереди**: ресурс дефицитный, раздаёт его третья сторона по опубликованным правилам, место нельзя купить и можно только уступить. Для библиотеки это новая семья. Ближайший сосед, «The Spend-By Date», выглядит похоже и устроен наоборот: там срок и деньги были наши, а неизвестным было прочтение правила, и потому первым шёл держатель правила.
Здесь правило опубликовано и читается за час. Неизвестно **наше собственное число**, и именно от него зависит, существует ли выбор вообще. Если разнесённый пик процесса не опускается под порог ничем, то разговаривать с оператором не о чем: остаётся очередь и четыре года. Если опускается — появляется вторая дорога, и только тогда вопрос к оператору имеет предмет. Первым идёт не самое срочное, а то, без чего второе не имеет смысла.
Возражение сильное, и оно не в том, что правила можно прочесть сегодня. Оно в другом: **получасовые записи принадлежат оператору, значит за данными и за ответом идут в одну и ту же дверь**. Верно — дверь одна, а разговоры разные. Записи выдают по заявке, не читая её; обязательство о месте в очереди дают против конкретной цифры, и цифру эту сначала надо получить и разобрать. Один визит, два разных разговора, и порядок между ними сохраняется.
Оператор вторым: его письменный ответ решает, стоит ли вообще считать конструкцию под порог или это выброшенные шесть недель. Техническая картина третья — она отсекает варианты сама, но отсекает по-разному в зависимости от второго ответа. Члены кооператива последними не потому, что менее важны: им предъявляется **уступка с ценой**, а до третьего шага цены нет, и разговор превращается в сбор тревоги.

feedback.top: You measured the site before asking anything of anybody, which is the order this problem rewards: the number decides whether a second road exists, and the members are shown a price rather than a worry.
feedback.mid: A workable order. One of the two things that decide whether the creamery can leave the queue at all comes early, and the case will hold together even if a month is lost finding that out.
feedback.low: This order carries the case to people and to the operator before the site has been measured, and in this problem the measurement is what says whether any of it is possible.

steps.prompt: Three numbers describe the same site. The creamery's own log, off the process switchboard, shows a winter peak of 480 kVA. The operator's half-hourly records, taken at the connection, show 610 kVA for the same week. The engineer's nameplate total lands far above either.

options.text: You lay the two winter records side by side and treat the 130 kVA between them as the load that is not on your switchboard.
options.fb: Two meters on one site disagreeing by a steady amount is not a problem to measure again; it is the answer. The gap has a name, and the name is the cold store.

options.text: You put sub-metering on the boiler house and the cold store for a fortnight, and hold every figure until the split is your own measurement.
options.fb: Sound instinct, and it buys with a fortnight what two records already on your desk will give you this afternoon.

options.text: You state plainly that the nameplate total is the conservative figure and build the case on that.
options.fb: Nameplates add up machines that never run in the same minute. Conservative here means far over the threshold, and over the threshold means four years.

options.text: You ask the operator which of the two site figures they would themselves use, and take that answer as the base.
options.fb: They will tell you they use their own records, which is true and stops one step short: it is the difference between the two that carries the information.

steps.prompt: Diversified, the electrified process peaks far above the small-works threshold, though across a winter day it averages well below it. The rules are explicit: a queue place is held while a reduced job is determined, and an amended application goes to the back of the batch. Everything rests on one physical question nobody has tested — whether a thermal store can carry a six-hour vat batch through the evening peak.

options.text: You have the store's discharge rate tested against a real batch before the road is chosen.
options.fb: Every month that follows is spent on an assumption nobody has put a meter on, and the rules re-date anyone who has to amend. A fortnight of testing buys the right to submit once.

options.text: You commit to the reduced road now and have the store tested as the design proceeds, since the calendar punishes waiting more than it punishes rework.
options.fb: The calendar does punish waiting. It punishes an amended application harder, and that is the one outcome this order makes likely.

options.text: You take the supplier's published performance figures as the test, which is what they are published for.
options.fb: Those figures are true of a store on a bench. Yours has to hold a vat through the hour the whole valley cooks its dinner.

options.text: You write to the operator and ask whether they have seen stores of this kind carry batch loads on other sites.
options.fb: They administer a queue; they do not commission thermal plant. The answer will be courteous, general, and no use in a determination.

steps.prompt: The store holds. That leaves two roads inside sixteen months. Work on your own ask until it goes under the threshold, which means a plant that runs constrained in the coldest weather. Or work on the queue: the poultry site ahead of you has held more capacity than the creamery needs since its own project was paused, and unused reservations can be reviewed on request.

options.text: You make the reduced ask the base case and keep the queue application alive behind it as the fallback.
options.fb: The road that depends on nobody else's decision becomes the plan; the road that runs through neighbours becomes the hedge. The rules hold your place while the smaller job is determined, so the hedge costs nothing to keep.

options.text: You go to the poultry site and ask what it would take for them to release capacity they are not using.
options.fb: Worth asking and it is not a plan: their answer is theirs to give, on their timetable, and the gas goes off on yours.

options.text: You ask the operator to review the reservations ahead of you, since the rules provide for it and the capacity is plainly idle.
options.fb: The rules do provide for it. They also do not hide who asked, and these farms live beside that site for the next ten years.

options.text: You have both roads designed in full and choose when the drawings are done.
options.fb: Two designs cost three of the sixteen months and answer a question the store test has already settled.

B1a.prompt: A reduced ask has a name the members will use: in the coldest fortnight the creamery would take in less milk than the farms produce. The chair of the members' committee wants to know what happens to that milk before he hears it from anyone else.

options.text: You give him the fortnight, the volume and the two ways it can be handled, and say which one you have not costed.
options.fb: He asked what happens to the milk. An answer with the unfinished part left visible is the only version he cannot be embarrassed by in six months.

options.text: You tell him the constraint is a design detail that will be engineered out long before it reaches a farm.
options.fb: It may well be engineered out. Said today it is a promise made for a design that does not exist, to a man who will repeat it tonight.

options.text: You explain that the alternative is four years without gas, so a fortnight of reduced intake is the cheap end of the choice.
options.fb: True, and it meets a question about the farms with an argument about the plant. The comparison lands once the fortnight has a number attached.

B1b.prompt: Word travels in a valley. Within a week the poultry site's manager is on the phone. He is not using the reservation and is unlikely to, but releasing it means telling his own board that the paused project is finished, and he would rather that sentence came out in his own time.

options.text: You ask what would let him keep the sentence in his own time and still let the capacity move.
options.fb: The obstacle is his board, not his capacity. Designing around the obstacle he actually has beats pressing the one he does not.

options.text: You tell him the capacity is idle, that everyone can see it is idle, and that you would rather he moved first.
options.fb: Everyone can see it is a threat with the verb removed, and you have told him the outcome is settled while asking him to choose it.

options.text: You thank him, close the conversation there, and put everything behind the reduced ask.
options.fb: Clean, and it leaves on the table a release he has not refused, only postponed.

options.text: You offer a joint statement that both sites are working with the operator on capacity in the valley.
options.fb: Cover is real currency and he has not asked for it yet. Meanwhile the statement moves no capacity at all.

steps.prompt: The store is being sized on last winter's half-hourly data. Last winter was the mildest in a decade, and in February the creamery ran a four-day week because a milk shortage left the vats half empty.

options.text: You rebuild the shape from the coldest fortnight in the ten-year record and ask what the plant would have drawn through it.
options.fb: A store is sized by the worst run it has to carry, not by the average of a kind year. The ten-year record holds that run; last winter does not.

options.text: You size on last winter and add a margin, taking the view that a margin set by engineers who know this plant beats a reconstructed fortnight.
options.fb: A margin is a guess wearing a number. It may land right, and nobody in the determination will be able to say why it is that size.

options.text: You use the ten-year average, which smooths out both the mild winter and the short February.
options.fb: Averaging removes exactly the fortnight the store exists for. The mean winter never has to be survived.

steps.prompt: Sized against the cold fortnight, the process comes to 760 kVA. The cold store's 130 sits on the same connection, which puts the ask over the threshold of 800. The cold store still has its own old supply, left in place a decade ago.

options.text: You put the cold store back on its own supply and submit the process ask at 760, with a written plan for the constrained fortnight.
options.fb: The kilovolt-amperes taking you over the line are the ones doing least for the mission, and they already have somewhere to go. Forty under the threshold is the whole difference between sixteen months and four years.

options.text: You buy the larger store, which carries the cold fortnight unconstrained and costs about a year of the members' dividend.
options.fb: It works, and it spends the members' money to buy back a fortnight they have never been asked whether they mind.

options.text: You submit at 799 and treat the shortfall on the coldest days as an operating matter for later.
options.fb: The figure is not a bid. It is what the relay will hold the site to, and the day it holds you the vats stop mid-batch.

options.text: You ask the members to accept reduced intake for two weeks a year and drop the store from the design altogether.
options.fb: Without the store two weeks becomes six, and you have asked them to accept a number nobody has calculated.

steps.prompt: The operator's connections engineer mentions, informally, a flexible connection: full capacity in nine months, ahead of the queue, but the network may curtail the site for up to two hundred hours a year at four hours' notice. A cheese vat cannot be stopped mid-batch, and a batch runs six hours.

options.text: You work out which hours a curtailment could fall in without killing a batch, and reply with the hours you can and cannot take.
options.fb: Two hundred hours is not a number, it is a shape. Answering with your own shape turns their offer into a negotiation instead of a coin toss.

options.text: You decline the flexible route and hold the reduced ask, which nobody can curtail.
options.fb: Firm capacity is worth a great deal here, and you closed the option before finding out whether the two hundred hours were movable at all.

options.text: You leave the offer where it is until the determination arrives, since one decision at a time is easier to defend to the board.
options.fb: The determination is three months away and the engineer's offer is informal, which is another way of saying it is still shapeable and will not stay so.

options.text: You ask for the offer in writing before your team spends an hour on it.
options.fb: Right to get it on paper before spending the team's week on it, and the engineer said it informally because informally is the stage at which terms still move.

B2a.prompt: Nothing in this valley stays quiet. Two other applicants learn that curtailment terms are being discussed at all and ask to be part of it. A request from three sites is harder for the operator to wave away and slower to assemble, and one of the three is the poultry site.

options.text: You agree to a joint request limited to the one term all three need, and keep your own timetable running underneath it.
options.fb: A coalition on one shared term is quick. A coalition on everything becomes a committee, and committees do not have gas going off in sixteen months.

options.text: You decline and keep the discussion to yourself, on the view that three timetables will never fit inside yours.
options.fb: The timetable risk is real, and you have paid for it in a currency the valley keeps count of.

options.text: You tell them you will share whatever terms you obtain, without making the request jointly.
options.fb: Generous and slightly hollow: terms are given to applicants, not published, and they will discover that after yours are settled.

B2b.prompt: The flexible connection goes no further, and in a small valley capacity not taken is itself news. The manager of a smallholding co-operative asks whether the creamery will support their objection to how the queue is administered, and mentions that their members are also your suppliers.

options.text: You ask to read the objection first, and tell him which parts of it you could sign and which you could not.
options.fb: He asked for support in the abstract. Reading it first is the only way to give an answer that survives the day it gets quoted back.

options.text: You sign it, since the same rules are about to be applied to your own determination.
options.fb: Your determination sits with the body being objected to, and you signed without reading what the objection actually says.

options.text: You decline and explain that the creamery cannot be seen to attack the process deciding its own application.
options.fb: An honest position, honestly given, and it ends the conversation with a supplier who came looking for an ally.

options.text: You offer to raise the points you agree with in your own correspondence with the operator, and to tell him which those are.
options.fb: It moves the substance without lending your name to a document you have not seen. He still leaves with nothing to show his members.

steps.prompt: Switchgear for the new intake runs fifteen months from order, and it cannot be ordered against a design that may still change. The determination takes up to three. The store takes six and can be built alongside anything. Fourteen months are left.

options.text: You place the switchgear order now against a break clause priced at about a month of the project's contingency.
options.fb: Fifteen and three do not fit inside fourteen end to end, and no amount of tidy sequencing makes them. The break clause is the price of the only order of events that lands in time.

options.text: You ask the manufacturer to hold a build slot without an order behind it.
options.fb: Ask by all means. A slot with nothing behind it is held right up until somebody else orders into it.

options.text: You wait for the determination and order the switchgear the week it arrives, so the members' money never goes into an unapproved design.
options.fb: Clean procurement and four months late. The gas goes off on a date that does not move for a tidy file.

options.text: You order the smaller unit available in six months, which suits the constrained design and nothing else.
options.fb: It arrives in good time to lock the creamery into the one design that has not been approved yet.

steps.prompt: At the members' meeting a farmer who also sits on the parish council says he has heard the creamery is getting its electricity ahead of everybody else in the valley. Sixty people are in the room, and the poultry site ahead of you employs eleven of their neighbours.

options.text: You explain what small works is, that it is open to any applicant under the threshold, and what the creamery gave up to get there.
options.fb: The rumour says you jumped a line. The answer is that you left it, at a price, by a door that is open to the poultry site too — checkable by anyone in the room.

options.text: You state that nobody has been overtaken and move the meeting on to the determination.
options.fb: True as far as it goes and it answers none of the feeling in the room, which will leave the meeting exactly as it arrived.

options.text: You set out the application from the first week and ask the room to judge whether the creamery has behaved well.
options.fb: Honest and one step too far: it hands sixty people a judgement that was yours to make and to defend.

steps.prompt: The determination arrives and it is conditional. Small works is granted if the site accepts a permanent import limit of 780 kVA, enforced by a relay at the intake — twenty above the ask. Beyond them the relay opens and the whole site goes off, vats included.

options.text: You accept, and put in an interlock that sheds the chilled-water plant before the relay ever sees the peak.
options.fb: A limit enforced by somebody else's relay is a limit the site should never reach. The interlock puts the last twenty kilovolt-amperes under your own control.
leads: лимит принят и своя защита поставлена

options.text: You accept and ask for the limit to be reviewed after two winters of measured data.
options.fb: Reasonable, and it leaves two winters in which the relay, not the review, decides what happens at the peak.

options.text: You accept and hold the limit by operating discipline, since the shift managers know this plant better than any relay does.
options.fb: Discipline holds until a chiller restarts during a wash cycle, and then the site is off with milk in the vats.

options.text: You accept, and set the site's own alarm and shed list at 770 so the shift sees the limit coming before the relay does.
options.fb: An alarm says it is happening. It does not say who may switch what off, and at 770 the shift has minutes rather than the interlock's seconds.
leads: лимит принят и своя защита поставлена

B3a.prompt: The relay is live and the first cold week comes early. On the Tuesday a wash cycle and a chiller restart land together and the site runs within four kilovolt-amperes of the limit. Nothing trips. The shift manager tells you afterwards that he watched it happen and did not know what he was allowed to turn off.

options.text: You work through the Tuesday with the shift and write down what may be shed and by whom before the next cold week.
options.fb: He was four kilovolt-amperes from stopping the site and had no authority he was sure of. The gap was never in the engineering; it was in what the shift had been told.

options.text: You take the decision out of the shift's hands entirely, since a relay does not care about pallets and cannot be argued with.
options.fb: Safe on paper. The next manager facing a lost pallet will find his way round a control he was never consulted about.

options.text: You watch for a month to see whether one Tuesday was one Tuesday.
options.fb: A month of watching is a month of running the coldest weeks of the year on nobody's judgement in particular.

options.text: You write the eleven minutes up for the operator before they find it in their own data.
options.fb: The right instinct about the operator, and it does nothing for the shift, who will meet the same Tuesday again on Thursday.

needs: лимит принят и своя защита поставлена

B3b.prompt: Before anything is signed the operator sends an acknowledgement for signature: the site accepts the consequences of a trip in the meantime. Your insurer reads the same sentence in the schedule of works and asks what has changed.

options.text: You take both letters to the board with what a trip would cost in lost milk, and let them sign one document knowing the number.
options.fb: Two counterparties are asking the same question in different languages. A board that signs with the cost in front of it has made a decision rather than a signature.

options.text: You sign the acknowledgement and tell the insurer separately that in practice the risk is unchanged.
options.fb: Two parties have now been told two things about one relay, and both of them keep their version in writing.

options.text: You publish the acknowledgement to the members before signing, so that nobody hears about the trip risk afterwards.
options.fb: Straight with the members and early by a step: they will ask what a trip costs, and that answer is not ready yet.

title: Listed and Lapsing
note: МАКЕТ. Сценарий, тексты и веса — наши. Ни одного числа, имени и формулировки PrepMatter (Ф3). Развилки ветвят по РОДУ хода (Ф21). Связывающее — ДВА ПРАВИЛА, КОТОРЫЕ НЕЛЬЗЯ СОБЛЮСТИ ОДНОВРЕМЕННО: два органа предъявляют требования, любое действие нарушает одно из них, и выигрывает не тот, кто выбрал сторону, а тот, кто заставил правила встретиться. Против восьми: 01 данные не сходятся · 02 законный календарь · 03 физическое окно · 04 чужие активы · 05 необратимость · 06 утраченное доверие · 07 деньги с датой · 08 место в чужой очереди. Ключ A>D>H>S: орган первым, потому что здесь правило живёт в УСМОТРЕНИИ, а не опубликовано механично, как в SFL-08. Ось величин — в шапке сборщика.

intro.head: Welcome to the Sustainable Futures Lab
intro.body: You have joined a small team advising a village-owned hydro scheme. You will make thirteen decisions. There is one clock for all of them, and you cannot go back.

intro.head: Background
intro.body: Ardenmill Hydro turns an 1892 weir into electricity for three hundred village shareholders. The weir is a listed structure. The abstraction licence comes up for renewal in thirteen months and will only be renewed with a working fish pass; the heritage authority has twice refused consent to alter the weir's fabric. Each body answers the same way when the other is mentioned: that is not our requirement to enforce. The scheme earns about £120,000 a year, thirty thousand of which keeps the village hall open.
intro.mission: Your mission: keep the licence and the listing, on a river with one construction window a year.

priorities.label: Get the two authorities to say, in one place, what each of them would accept
Settle which fish count the licence will actually be measured against
Work out which of the three passes can be built in the window that is left
Take the shareholders through what each road costs them before it is chosen

steps.prompt: Put these four actions in the order you would take them, starting with the one you would do first.
steps.why:
Связывающее здесь — **два правила, которые нельзя соблюсти одновременно**. Не срок, не деньги и не чужая очередь: два органа предъявляют требования, любое действие нарушает одно из них, и ни один из двух не считает чужое требование своей заботой.
Орган первым — и это **не тот же ход, что в SFL-08, а обратный ему**. Там правило было опубликовано и механично: порог малых работ либо взят, либо нет, и неизвестным было наше собственное число. Здесь оба правила живут в **усмотрении**: охрана отказала дважды конкретному проекту, а не любому; у лицензии есть оговорка о соразмерности. Пока не сказано, что каждый из двух считает выполнением, и данные, и проект считаются вслепую — можно построить безупречный рыбоход, который не примет ни один из них.
Возражение сильное, и оно очевидное: **идти к органу без проекта — значит получить отписку**. Верно, если идёшь с вопросом «что вам понравится». Неверно, если идёшь с вопросом «какая из трёх дорог для вас недопустима и почему» — на него отвечают, и ответ снимает половину работы, которую иначе делают впустую.
Данные вторыми: подсчёты расходятся в два с лишним раза, и от того, какой из них признан, зависит, нужен ли вообще самый дорогой проход. Техническая картина третья — она отсекает варианты сама, но по-разному в зависимости от первых двух ответов. Пайщики последними не потому, что менее важны: им предъявляется **счёт с ценой**, а до третьего шага цены нет, и собрание превращается в сбор страхов.

feedback.top: You go to the two bodies before building anything, because the requirement here is not written down anywhere in a form you can build against, and everything after that is measured against what they say.
feedback.mid: A workable order: one of the two things that decide what may even be built comes early, and the scheme will reach the window with a case rather than a drawing.
feedback.low: This order designs and consults before either authority has said what it would accept, and in this problem neither requirement exists in a buildable form until they do.

steps.prompt: Both authorities have now written to you. The licensing body says a pass must be in place at renewal and that consents are a matter for the applicant. The heritage body says the fabric is not to be altered and that abstraction is not its concern. Neither letter mentions the other.

options.text: You put all three passes in one paper to both bodies and ask each to say which it could not accept.
options.fb: Neither of them will resolve a conflict they have not been shown. One paper, both addressees, a question each can answer without conceding anything — that is how the two requirements first appear on the same page.

options.text: You ask the licensing body for an extension while the heritage question is worked out.
options.fb: Extensions are granted against a plan. Asked with nothing behind it, the request tells them the scheme has thirteen months and no design.

options.text: You take the heritage refusal as settled, since it has already been given twice, and design only what leaves the fabric untouched.
options.fb: Probably where you end up, and you have thrown away the reason for the refusals without reading it. Twice refused is not the same as never permissible.

options.text: You commission the design first, so that whatever you send them is a real proposal rather than three sketches.
options.fb: A real proposal takes four months and can be refused for a reason you could have been told in a fortnight.

steps.prompt: Two counts of the same river disagree. The trap on the old fish ladder recorded 1,900 fish last season. The eDNA survey commissioned by the angling club estimates 4,600. The licence condition is that ninety per cent of migrating fish can pass.

options.text: You ask the licensing body which count its condition is written against, before either number goes into a design.
options.fb: Ninety per cent of what is the whole question. The body that wrote the condition is the only one whose answer binds, and it costs a letter to have it.

options.text: You design against the higher figure, since a pass sized for 4,600 also carries 1,900.
options.fb: Safe on capacity and it may buy a structure the river does not need, which on this weir is the difference between touching the fabric and not.

options.text: You take the trap count, which is a physical record rather than a modelled estimate.
options.fb: A trap counts what came to the trap. The ladder it sits on is the very thing everyone agrees fish are avoiding.

options.text: You commission a third count to break the tie.
options.fb: A third number arrives in a season and settles nothing: nobody has yet said which kind of number the condition means.

steps.prompt: The licensing body replies that the condition is written against the eDNA estimate. The heritage officer replies that her objection was to the notch cut in the crest, not to a pass as such. Two roads open. Bring both bodies into one determination, which nobody has asked for and neither has refused. Or go to each in turn with the road that suits it, and carry the difference yourself.

options.text: You propose one joint meeting, one paper, one set of drawings, and offer to write the note yourself.
options.fb: The conflict lives between two desks and cannot be resolved on either of them. Offering to write the note is what makes a meeting nobody owns actually happen.

options.text: You go to the heritage officer first, since her objection is the narrower one and she has just told you what it was.
options.fb: Sensible order, and it leaves you carrying each body's answer to the other, translated by the party with an interest in the translation.

options.text: You go to the licensing body first and ask it to state its condition in terms the heritage officer can respond to.
options.fb: It will restate the condition in its own terms, which is what it has already done twice in writing.

options.text: You write to the department above both of them and ask it to direct the two.
options.fb: Going over two heads in month five buys a letter in month nine and two officials who now read everything you send twice.

B1a.prompt: The two officials are in the same room for the first time, and it is polite and slow. Forty minutes in, neither has said anything that could be written down as a requirement, and the heritage officer has twice referred to the weir as a monument rather than a structure.

options.text: You put the three drawings on the table and ask each of them to say aloud what would have to change for the answer to be yes.
options.fb: Politeness in a room like this is the absence of a written question. Asking for the condition of a yes turns two positions into two lists you can build against.

options.text: You let the meeting run its course and write up what you heard, sending it to both for correction.
options.fb: The write-up is worth having and it puts the burden of precision on two people who have just spent forty minutes avoiding it.

options.text: You say the scheme has thirteen months and that without a decision today the village loses the hall as well as the licence.
options.fb: The hall is real and it is not their problem, and you have just told two regulators that the pressure on you is greater than the pressure on them.

B1b.prompt: Working the two desks separately is doing what it does. The heritage officer has given you an oral steer she will not put in writing, and the licensing case officer has asked, twice, what the heritage position is. Whatever you tell each of them now, you are the only witness to what the other said.

options.text: You write down what each told you, send each note to its author for correction, and copy nothing to the other until it is confirmed.
options.fb: The risk in shuttle work is not lying, it is remembering conveniently. A note corrected by its own author survives the day the two of them finally speak.

options.text: You tell the licensing officer what the heritage steer was, since he has now asked twice and the delay is starting to look like evasion.
options.fb: He asked and it was not yours to give: the steer was oral because she is not ready to own it, and now she will hear her position quoted by a third party.

options.text: You tell each of them only what is already in writing, and say plainly that the rest is oral and not yours to pass on.
options.fb: Clean and a little slow. It leaves the case officer with a gap he will fill with his own assumption about what she said.

steps.prompt: The eDNA estimate covers the whole river above and below the weir, across the season. The licence condition speaks of ninety per cent of migrating fish. Salmon run in two autumn weeks; eels move through most of the summer; both are in the estimate.

options.text: You ask which species the condition is written for and get the answer before the pass is sized for either.
options.fb: A pass built for eels is not a pass built for salmon, and the same number covers both in the estimate. One question separates two designs.

options.text: You size for both, since a pass that carries salmon and eels satisfies any reading of the condition.
options.fb: It satisfies every reading and it is the largest structure of the three, which is exactly what the heritage officer objects to.

options.text: You take salmon as the intended species, since they are the run the licence was written around historically.
options.fb: Probably right and stated by you rather than by them. On this river the eel numbers are the ones that moved.

options.text: You split the estimate by species yourself from the survey's raw returns.

intro.head: Welcome to the Sustainable Futures Lab
intro.body: You have joined a small team advising a community-owned water company. You will make thirteen decisions. There is one clock for all of them, and you cannot go back.

intro.head: Background
intro.body: Cavanmoor Water is owned by the nine hundred households it supplies, and draws everything it sells from one chalk aquifer. The aquifer refills at about four megalitres a day. The company takes 4.6 — three and a half for the town, 1.1 for a maltings that employs sixty people. The difference has been coming out of storage for four years and has widened as demand rose: 200 of the 900 megalitres of buffer are gone. If the water table at the monitoring borehole passes twelve metres below datum, the chalk stream it feeds stops flowing in August and the regulator cuts the licence by a quarter, permanently. The table stands at 9.4 metres and falls about 0.8 a year.
intro.mission: Your mission: still be taking water in twenty years, from a bank that refills more slowly than the town spends it.

priorities.label: Start the one measure that closes the gap for good, before its lead time runs out
Get the regulator to state exactly what it measures the twelve-metre threshold against
Establish how much buffer is really left and how fast it is going
Put the choice to the households who own the company and to the maltings

steps.prompt: Put these four actions in the order you would take them, starting with the one you would do first.
steps.why:
Связывающее здесь — **запас, который делишь с самим собой через время**. Он возобновляемый, но медленнее, чем расходуется, и за порогом потеря становится вечной. Это новая семья: в «Peatland Baseline» необратимой была разовая операция, здесь необратим **накопленный перебор**, набегающий по капле.
И порядок здесь **обратный тому, чему учат восемь предыдущих сценариев**. Обычно первым идёт замер: пока не знаешь своего числа, любой ход слепой. Здесь замер вторичен, и вот почему. Единственный рычаг, который меняет баланс навсегда, — программа утечек: она даёт 0.7 против дефицита 0.6, то есть переводит минус в плюс. **Её срок — три года. До порога — три с четвертью.** Любая неделя, потраченная до её запуска, вычитается не из комфорта, а из единственного решения, которое вообще существует.
Возражение сильное и его надо назвать: **запускать программу на £2.4 млн, не зная точно, сколько осталось буфера, — это трата вслепую**. Оно верно ровно наполовину. Замер уточнит, три года у нас или четыре; он не изменит того, что программа нужна при любом из этих ответов и что раньше чем через три года она не сработает. **Когда срок исполнения длиннее остатка, порядок задаётся сроком, а не точностью.**
Регулятор вторым: от того, что именно он мерит за порог — уровень в скважине или августовский расход ручья, — зависит, три года у нас или пять. Замер третьим: он уточняет темп, а не решение. Домохозяйства последними: им предъявляется счёт с ценой, а до третьего шага цены нет.

intro.head: Welcome to the Sustainable Futures Lab
intro.body: You have joined a small team advising a council-owned recycling company. You will make thirteen decisions. There is one clock for all of them, and you cannot go back.

intro.head: Background
intro.body: Marden Resource Recovery is paid £62 a tonne for every tonne it keeps out of landfill, under a ten-year contract with the council of which four years have gone. It diverted 41,000 tonnes last year — £2.54m against fixed costs of £2.1m — and it did its job so well that the town now throws away less every year. Total waste is falling about 9 per cent a year as reuse and repair spread, and the company's income falls with it. The contract has one mid-term review, and it opens in seven months. Sixty people work here.
intro.mission: Your mission: keep the company alive on the strength of the very thing that is closing it.

priorities.label: Get the council to reopen how the company is paid, at the one review it has
Establish how fast the tonnage really falls and what it does to the surplus
Tell sixty people what is happening before the figures reach them another way
Work out what the company could be paid for instead of tonnes

steps.prompt: Put these four actions in the order you would take them, starting with the one you would do first.
steps.why:
Связывающее — **успех, который ломает механизм**. Компанию платят за тонну, отведённую от полигона; она отводит так хорошо, что тонн становится меньше, и доход падает **ровно потому, что работа сделана**. Это новая семья: в «The Spend-By Date» деньги сгорали по календарю, здесь они тают от собственного результата.
Совет первым — и не потому, что он главный, а потому что **у рычага одна дата**. Среднесрочный пересмотр открывается через семь месяцев и бывает единожды за десять лет; пропустить его — значит шесть лет жить по формуле, которая наказывает за работу. Всё остальное можно сделать позже, эту дверь позже открыть нельзя.
Возражение сильное: **идти к плательщику без числа — получить отписку**, и наша же библиотека учит сначала мерить. Верно наполовину. К пересмотру идут не с числом, а с **заявкой на пересмотр**: она процедурная, подаётся заранее и стоит письма. Число нужно к слушанию, а не к заявке, и оно вторым.
Данные вторыми: падение тонн и падение излишка — разные скорости, и от их разницы зависит, о чём просить. Люди третьими: шестьдесят человек узнают из городской газеты, если мы будем ждать готового ответа. Новая формула последней — и возражение к этому сильнее прочих: **как просить пересмотр, не зная, за что хочешь получать**. Отвечаю: к слушанию форма нужна, и к шагам 4 и 7 она появится. Но написанная до заявки, она превращает пересмотр в защиту своей конструкции; написанная после — остаётся предметом торга, каким и должна быть.

feedback.top: You file for the review first because it opens once in ten years, and bring the number to the hearing rather than to the letter.
feedback.mid: Workable. The review is not last, and the company will reach the hearing with something to say.
feedback.low: This order designs a new payment mechanism before asking whether the payer will hear one, and the door that matters opens once.

steps.prompt: The review has to be requested in writing, and the clerk says requests are usually made by the council, not by the contractor. Nothing in the contract says the contractor cannot ask. The window opens in seven months and closes six weeks later.

options.text: You file the request now in plain terms and say the case will follow.
options.fb: Filing is procedural and costs a letter; the case is an argument and costs three months. Doing them in that order is what keeps both.

options.text: You ask the clerk what a contractor's request has to contain before you send anything.
options.fb: Careful and it spends two weeks discovering that the answer is «a request». The form here is thinner than the fear of it.

options.text: You wait until the surplus figures for the year are audited, so the request lands with evidence behind it.
options.fb: Evidence belongs at the hearing. The audit lands two months after the window closes.

options.text: You raise it informally with the cabinet member and let her decide whether to open the review.
options.fb: She may well open it, and you have made the one dated lever in the contract depend on somebody remembering a conversation.

steps.prompt: Tonnage collected is down 12 per cent on last year while the town's total waste fell about 9. The finance officer reads the 12 as the trend. Two of the four rounds changed to fortnightly collection in the same year, and a large employer closed in the spring.

options.text: You separate the fall into what the town stopped throwing away and what left the town.
options.fb: One of the two is your success and the other is somebody's redundancy. Asking the council to change a formula means knowing which is which.

options.text: You take the 9 per cent as it stands, since it is the number the council will use anyway.
options.fb: They will use it, and at the hearing you will be arguing about a number you have not taken apart.

options.text: You model three scenarios from 5 to 12 per cent and present the range.
options.fb: A range is honest and it postpones the question the range exists to answer: which part of the fall is permanent.

options.text: You commission a waste-composition study of the whole district.
options.fb: Nine months and a large invoice for a question your own weighbridge tickets can answer by round.

steps.prompt: Two ways to be paid for something other than tonnes. A payment for outcomes the council actually wants — waste avoided, materials kept in use — which nobody in the county has yet written into a contract. Or a floor under the existing rate, which is familiar, quick, and leaves the perverse formula intact.

options.text: You put the floor and the outcome payment into a single paper, one as the ask and one as the direction.
options.fb: The floor is what the council can grant in six weeks; the direction is what stops you being here again in year eight. One paper keeps them from being traded against each other.

options.text: You put the outcome payment alone, since a floor rewards the same wrong thing more gently and buys six quiet years.
options.fb: Right about the formula and it asks a council with six weeks to invent a contract type the county has never used.

options.text: You ask only for the floor and leave the mechanism for the next contract.
options.fb: It buys six years of the same perverse formula, and the next contract is negotiated by whoever is here then.

options.text: You ask for the contract to be terminated early and retendered on a new basis.
options.fb: Termination is the one door that cannot be reopened, offered to a council that has not yet been asked for the cheap thing.

B1a.prompt: The finance officer reads the paper and picks up the floor immediately: it is a number she can put in a budget line. She has not mentioned the second half, and the hearing is in five weeks.

options.text: You thank her for the floor and ask what would have to be true for the second half to be piloted on one round.
options.fb: She took what she could use. A pilot on one round is the smallest version of the second half that still exists after the hearing.

options.text: You press for both together, since separating them is how the direction gets lost between one budget round and the next.
options.fb: Pressing a person who has just said yes to something is how the yes gets reopened.

options.text: You accept the floor and put the outcome payment into the next contract's brief.
options.fb: Clean and it moves the argument to a document nobody has started, to be read by people not yet appointed.

B1b.prompt: By the end of the week two versions of the paper are circulating at the depot, and neither of them is the paper. One says the contract is being torn up; the other says the tonnage bonus is going.

options.text: You tell the depot in one sentence what the paper actually asks for.
options.fb: Rumour beats you to the floor whenever the true account is longer than the false one. One sentence travels; a briefing does not.

options.text: You call an all-staff meeting for the following week and set out the whole position.
options.fb: The right meeting, seven days after the week in which people decide what they believe.

options.text: You say nothing until the council answers, since half the versions will be wrong either way.
options.fb: Both versions are already moving, and silence is read as confirmation of whichever one frightens people more.

steps.prompt: The company's case rests on a claim that reuse is displacing waste. The evidence is the town's two repair cafés and a furniture reuse shop, whose own records count items rather than tonnes, and count them at the point of donation.

options.text: You weigh a sample of their items instead of assuming an average weight.
options.fb: A sofa and a toaster are one item each. The council will test this number harder than any other in the paper, because it is the one that asks them for money.

options.text: You use published average weights per item category.
options.fb: Defensible and borrowed. The first question at the hearing will be whether those averages are from a town like this one.

options.text: You drop the reuse claim and argue on tonnage alone.
options.fb: It is the strongest part of the story and the hardest to prove, and dropping it leaves you arguing that success looks like decline.

options.text: You ask the reuse shop to start recording weights from next month, so that next year's case rests on measurement.
options.fb: Good for next year's case. The hearing is in five weeks.

steps.prompt: The floor can be set two ways. At the current £2.54m, which freezes today's income for six years and asks the council for the most. Or at fixed costs plus a margin — £2.3m — which is defensible line by line and gives up £240,000 of a surplus that is £440,000.

options.text: You ask for the defensible figure with the working shown, and name what the difference buys.
options.fb: A number the council can defend in public survives its own finance committee. Naming what the difference buys is what stops it being read as a discount.

options.text: You ask for the current income and let them negotiate down.
options.fb: Standard practice and it invites the committee to find its own number, which will be below both of yours.

options.text: You ask for costs plus a margin and say the pilot will be funded separately.
options.fb: Two asks in two papers, the second of which arrives after the review window has closed.

options.text: You ask for a floor indexed to the town's total waste, so it falls more slowly than income.
options.fb: An index tied to the very thing you are trying to reduce, explained to a committee in six weeks.

steps.prompt: A week before the hearing the council's waste officer says privately that the cabinet will not grant a floor in an election year, but might fund a pilot. The floor is the part that keeps sixty people employed; the pilot is the part that changes the formula.

options.text: You go into the hearing with both and let the cabinet choose in public which one it is refusing.
options.fb: A refusal made in the room is a decision with a name on it. Withdrawing the floor in advance saves them from ever making it.

options.text: You drop the floor and ask only for the pilot, taking the officer's read as good and saving the cabinet a public refusal.
options.fb: His read is probably right, and you have conceded the employment case to a corridor conversation with no author.

options.text: You ask for the floor alone and hold the pilot for a calmer year.
options.fb: It protects the sixty and leaves the formula intact for the six years in which it does its damage.

options.text: You ask the officer to put his read in writing before you decide anything.
options.fb: He will decline, politely, and the week you spent asking was the week to rewrite the paper.

B2a.prompt: The hearing is public and three of the town's repair and reuse groups have asked whether they should attend. They are the evidence for half the case and they have never spoken at a council committee.

options.text: You invite them and ask each for one specific thing they have seen, rather than support for the company.
options.fb: A committee discounts an ally speaking for a contractor and cannot discount a resident describing a Saturday. The narrower the testimony, the harder it is to wave away.

options.text: You invite them and brief them on the company's argument so the messages align.
options.fb: Aligned messages read as coached, and the one thing they have that you do not is that nobody pays them.

options.text: You thank them and keep the hearing to the company, to avoid the appearance of a lobby.
options.fb: Defensible, and it keeps out of the room the only voices whose interest is not financial.

B2b.prompt: Whatever went in, the paper is now narrower than what the depot was told. The shop steward asks, in front of the shift, whether the sixty jobs are in the paper at all.

options.text: You say what is in the paper and what is not, and why the second was left out.
options.fb: He asked a question with a yes-or-no shape and a real answer behind it. Giving the reason is what stops the answer becoming the rumour.

options.text: You say the jobs are safe while the contract runs, which is true for six years.
options.fb: True, and it answers a question about the paper with a fact about the contract, in front of people who can tell the difference.

options.text: You promise to take the jobs question back to the board before the hearing.
options.fb: A real commitment made to buy the end of a difficult conversation, with five days to keep it.
